interest: Shows State's private doubt that Japan's land reform could survive without post-treaty U.S. enforcement leverage.
overview: A 1949 State memo and MacArthur's published letter to Yoshida mark the land reform's third anniversary; the memo worries the draft Peace Treaty gives the U.S. no post-treaty tools beyond diplomacy to prevent reform reversal, while MacArthur urges continued vigilance against pre-war tenancy.

subfiles.about: A memorandum reporting consultations with John Allison on U.S. policy regarding Japanese land reform and the lack of post-treaty enforcement mechanisms under the draft Japanese Peace Treaty.
subfiles.summary: Memo tells Jessup that Allison shared MacArthur's land-reform letter and FE's instruction backing it, but warns the draft Peace Treaty gives the U.S. no post-treaty authority over Japanese land tenure beyond routine diplomacy.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from CWY to Mr. Jessup on Land Reform in Japan and Post-Treaty Controls

subfiles.about: A letter from General Douglas MacArthur to Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida commemorating the third anniversary of Japan's land reform legislation and urging vigilance to prevent reversion to pre-reform land tenure.
subfiles.summary: Marking land reform's third anniversary, MacArthur praises rural Japan's success, calls it a model democratic achievement, and warns continued vigilance, enforcement, and local agricultural commissions are needed to prevent reverting to pre-war tenancy.
subfiles.title: Letter from Douglas MacArthur to Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida on Land Reform
